drafted_from: tool:save-tool's port of the old server's saveTool (b6ae0ebf815f, src/workshop.mjs:1455); the row shape of tool:sales-contracts
start_here: Say to your AI: "Save this tool so I can find it later: <descriptor and files>." It checks the tool the same way a catalog tool is checked, then keeps it as one row of the saved_tools table in the database you name.
no_lists_because: A saved tool is one row of the saved_tools table in the database the person names (the tool makes that table on first use), not a row of a list, so there is no list for a person to keep or pour into.
instructions: 1. Give your AI the tool's descriptor (its id, job, input_schema and invoke) and its code as files, for example {"main.py": "..."}.
2. Name the database the tool is kept in. The first save makes the saved_tools table there.
3. Read the answer: the saved id, its fingerprint and its size. A refused save names each problem in plain words; fix those and save again.

worked_examples.title: Keep a small echo tool
worked_examples.ask: Save this tool so I can find it later: it echoes text back.
worked_examples.given: A descriptor for tool:echo-test and its one file, main.py
worked_examples.hands_back: The saved id tool:echo-test, its fingerprint beginning 1f:, its size in bytes and saved: true; the table is saved_tools
